source.title: AdaR: An Adaptive Gradient Method with Cyclical Restarting of Moment Estimations
source.authors: Yang-Chuan Wang; Lianhong Ding; Peng Shi

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Table 4's heading names LSTM results on PTB, but its table values are not reliably attributable to PTB or another model from the flattened text; those values are omitted.
record.tranche_reason: Compares a new adaptive optimizer with Adam and SGD on held-out image-classification and language-modeling performance, using the same generalization outcome but a different optimizer intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on natural-label datasets. These results bear on V4; it does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, large-batch penalties, dropout effects, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. AdaR's own restart-interval and step-size ablations are not separate claim-version results.
record.test_reason: The optimizer comparisons directly measure V4's held-out performance differences on image and language tasks. Adam versus momentum SGD tests the adaptive-method disadvantage; AdaR tests how modifying an adaptive optimizer changes that comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion that restarting moment estimates mitigates distant-gradient influence and improves step-size adaptation, convergence and generalization. Their broad superiority statement needs the reported MNIST exception: AdaR slightly trails SGD there. The experiments report performance differences but do not independently establish the proposed causal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: AdaR adds cyclical restarting of Adam moment estimates; it is compared with Adam, other adaptive methods, and SGD. The paper reports grid searches for optimal parameters across tasks, with shared image-task settings for adaptive methods.
record.method_sensitivity: AdaR's interval length and step size are ablated; the authors report favorable performance across the tested interval lengths and step sizes. The paper recommends an interval length of 12.
record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-25), Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: Each method is run 3 times with the best result reported, so the reported comparisons do not provide variability estimates. Table 4's flattened presentation prevents reliable assignment of its displayed perplexity values. Table 2's ResNet-34 accuracy conflicts with the pairwise improvements stated in the prose.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4's LSTM training/test perplexity values are omitted because the flattened table text does not preserve reliable optimizer-to-value assignments. The text's explicit qualitative statement that AdaR has the lowest training and test perplexities is retained in R9 with values not stated.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

A controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. The reported search includes momentum and Adam moment coefficients as well as learning rates, so it does not isolate the learning-rate-and-schedule-only regime.
Batch-size comparisons and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Effects of adding or removing dropout; dropout settings are held fixed within optimizer comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: Separate optimizer-specific comparisons, including the other adaptive baselines. Their results show substantial variation: on CIFAR-10 ResNet-34, NosAdam and Adam Win also beat SGD; on WikiText-2, AdaPlus beats SGD while AdaBound, NosAdam and Adam Win trail it.

Training perplexities for the WikiText-2 comparison: Adam 37.94, SGD 149.41 and AdaR 88.52. Adam's better training performance alongside worse test performance directly bears on V4's training-versus-generalization distinction.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. All results are the best of three runs, with no variability estimates. Each extracted row combines optimizer comparisons with different directions, so its single state describes AdaR versus SGD; the verdicts also use the explicitly recorded Adam-versus-SGD baselines. Table 4 is recoverable from the supplied text, and its omission was already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Other adaptive optimizers and broader tuning; the paper compares AdaR and selected optimizers, not the full range of tuning regimes or all benchmarks in the version.
Large-batch versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with training-set size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
